Bench Pullover

Pullover works lats as well as chest and triceps depending on where we are on the range of motion. Holding the inside face of the dumbbell is going to allow for a better grip as well as protraction and elevation of the shoulders to engage serratus a bit better. When we get to the further end of range of motion, it’s even more imperative to keep a neutral spine. If members need, we can always elevate the feet to help seat the lower back better. Keep the arms long with a very soft, non-changing angle of the elbow, hinging from the shoulder joint.

Bench Seated Low Row

The more parallel we can be to the ground, the easier it will be to truly engage the lats. Many members will find it hard to breathe or maybe not even get close to that position due to tightness in the hamstrings or lower back. Most will find more of a 45° angle. 
Coach Tony @konidaris1207 gives a great cue of moving the dumbbells back like an escalator. Many also respond well to cueing pulling the elbows back behind the hips because regardless of torso angle they will reduce trap dominance and engage lats. Try and use them both. Share in the comments if you have any other cues that work well.

Y-Raise: Most OTF exercises ask for shoulder blades to be back and down (retracted and depressed). This is one of the few movements that actually call for scapular elevation and upward rotation. If we get members into a great starting position, it doesn’t take an aggressive angle to challenge the movement. Let’s have them actively drive the hands away from the shoulders.
